max_results=100000 < 10 * n_conformers=203812860 (pitfall 12: per-batch truncation)  [KNOWN HARNESS DEFECT, T69: this advisory demands max_results >= 10 * n_conformers, i.e. k >= 203812860 here, which a device-resident top-K cannot be asked for -- the condition is unsatisfiable, not unmet. The pitfall it guards (roshambo2's shipped 10,000 applied PER BATCH before merging) is addressed by setting max_results explicitly on BOTH sides, which this session does.]

CUDA toolkit 12.9 is not the pinned 13.2. The toolkit version is a measured arithmetic axis: 13.2 vs 12.9 leaves 92.95% of pairs bit-identical, with |dT_shape| p99 = 8.9e-8 and max = 3.0e-7 on the rest (T03, sm_120). Scores from this build are not bitwise comparable with scores from the pinned toolkit.  [EXPECTED AND UNAVOIDABLE: CUDA 13.x dropped sm_70 outright, so a TITAN V build can only be made on 12.x. This is the matched-architecture comparison D023 licenses tachi for, and it is a wall-clock ratio between two tools on one card -- not a score compared against an sm_120 number. No score from this run is combined with a score taken under the pinned toolkit.]

build library molecules '70-real', which does not include the architecture this policy's numbers were measured on (sm_120). Scores from it are not bitwise comparable with scores taken on sm_120: T25 measured sm_70 vs sm_120 as bit-identical at a fixed pose but |dT_shape| p99 = 2.6e-5 after 100 Adagrad steps (results/T25/, decisions/D001).  [EXPECTED AND THE POINT: the whole reason for running on tachi is that its TITAN V is the GPU model the comparison paper benchmarked. Same disposition as the toolkit advisory above: a wall-clock ratio on one card, no cross-architecture score claim.]
